005package org.wpilib.command3.sysid;
006
007import static org.wpilib.units.Units.Second;
008import static org.wpilib.units.Units.Seconds;
009import static org.wpilib.units.Units.Volts;
010import static org.wpilib.util.ErrorMessages.requireNonNullParam;
011
012import java.util.function.Consumer;
013import org.wpilib.command3.Command;
014import org.wpilib.command3.Mechanism;
015import org.wpilib.sysid.SysIdRoutineLog;
016import org.wpilib.system.Timer;
017import org.wpilib.units.VoltageUnit;
018import org.wpilib.units.measure.Time;
019import org.wpilib.units.measure.Velocity;
020import org.wpilib.units.measure.Voltage;

022/**
023 * A SysId characterization routine for a single mechanism. Mechanisms may have multiple motors.
024 *
025 * <p>A single subsystem may have multiple mechanisms, but mechanisms should not share test
026 * routines. Each complete test of a mechanism should have its own SysIdRoutine instance, since the
027 * log name of the recorded data is determined by the mechanism name.
028 *
029 * <p>The test state (e.g. "quasistatic-forward") is logged once per iteration during test
030 * execution, and once with state "none" when a test ends. Motor frames are logged every iteration
031 * during test execution.
032 *
033 * <p>Timestamps are not coordinated across data, so motor frames and test state tags may be
034 * recorded on different log frames. Because frame alignment is not guaranteed, SysId parses the log
035 * by using the test state flag to determine the timestamp range for each section of the test, and
036 * then extracts the motor frames within the valid timestamp ranges. If a given test was run
037 * multiple times in a single logfile, the user will need to select which of the tests to use for
038 * the fit in the analysis tool.
039 *
040 * <p>This class is provided by the Commands v3 VendorDep
041 */
042public class SysIdRoutine extends SysIdRoutineLog {
043  private final Config m_config;
044  private final SysIdMechanism m_mechanism;
045  private final Consumer<State> m_recordState;
046
047  /**
048   * Create a new SysId characterization routine.
049   *
050   * @param config Hardware-independent parameters for the SysId routine.
051   * @param mechanism Hardware interface for the SysId routine.
052   */
053  public SysIdRoutine(Config config, SysIdMechanism mechanism) {
054    super(mechanism.name);
055    m_config = config;
056    m_mechanism = mechanism;
057    m_recordState = config.recordState != null ? config.recordState : this::recordState;
058  }
059
060  /** Hardware-independent configuration for a SysId test routine. */
061  public static class Config {
062    /** The voltage ramp rate used for quasistatic test routines. */
063    public final Velocity<VoltageUnit> rampRate;
064
065    /** The step voltage output used for dynamic test routines. */
066    public final Voltage stepVoltage;
067
068    /** Safety timeout for the test routine commands. */
069    public final Time timeout;
070
071    /** Optional handle for recording test state in a third-party logging solution. */
072    public final Consumer<State> recordState;
073
074    /** Default voltage ramp rate used in quasistatic test routines, set to 1 volt per second. */
075    public static final Velocity<VoltageUnit> DEFAULT_RAMP_RATE = Volts.of(1).per(Second);
076
077    /** Default step voltage used in dynamic test routines, set to 7 volts. */
078    public static final Voltage DEFAULT_STEP_VOLTAGE = Volts.of(7);
079
080    /** Default timeout used to automatically end test routine commands, set to 10 seconds. */
081    public static final Time DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = Seconds.of(10);
082
083    /**
084     * Create a new configuration for a SysId test routine. To use the default config values, pass
085     * in the provided static default fields.
086     *
087     * @param rampRate The voltage ramp rate used for quasistatic test routines.
088     * @param stepVoltage The step voltage output used for dynamic test routines.
089     * @param timeout Safety timeout for the test routine commands.
090     * @param recordState Optional handle for recording test state in a third-party logging
091     *     solution. If provided, the test routine state will be passed to this callback instead of
092     *     logged in WPILog.
093     */
094    public Config(
095        Velocity<VoltageUnit> rampRate,
096        Voltage stepVoltage,
097        Time timeout,
098        Consumer<State> recordState) {
099      requireNonNullParam(rampRate, "rampRate", "SysIdRoutine.Config");
100      requireNonNullParam(stepVoltage, "stepVoltage", "SysIdRoutine.Config");
101      requireNonNullParam(timeout, "timeout", "SysIdRoutine.Config");
102      this.rampRate = rampRate;
103      this.stepVoltage = stepVoltage;
104      this.timeout = timeout;
105      this.recordState = recordState;
106    }
107
108    /**
109     * Create a new configuration for a SysId test routine.
110     *
111     * @param rampRate The voltage ramp rate used for quasistatic test routines.
112     * @param stepVoltage The step voltage output used for dynamic test routines.
113     * @param timeout Safety timeout for the test routine commands.
114     * @return A Config object with the specified ramp rate, step voltage, and timeout that records
115     *     to a DataLog file.
116     */
117    public static Config useDataLog(
118        Velocity<VoltageUnit> rampRate, Voltage stepVoltage, Time timeout) {
119      return new Config(rampRate, stepVoltage, timeout, null);
120    }
121
122    /**
123     * Create a default configuration for a SysId test routine with all default settings.
124     *
125     * <p>rampRate: 1 volt/sec
126     *
127     * <p>stepVoltage: 7 volts
128     *
129     * <p>timeout: 10 seconds
130     *
131     * @return A Config object with the default ramp rate, step voltage, and timeout that records to
132     *     a DataLog file.
133     */
134    public static Config defaults() {
135      return new Config(DEFAULT_RAMP_RATE, DEFAULT_STEP_VOLTAGE, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT, null);
136    }
137  }
138
139  /**
140   * A mechanism to be characterized by a SysId routine. Defines callbacks needed for the SysId test
141   * routine to control and record data from the mechanism.
142   */
143  public static class SysIdMechanism {
144    /** Sends the SysId-specified drive signal to the mechanism motors during test routines. */
145    public final Consumer<? super Voltage> drive;
146
147    /**
148     * Returns measured data (voltages, positions, velocities) of the mechanism motors during test
149     * routines.
150     */
151    public final Consumer<SysIdRoutineLog> log;
152
153    /** The mechanism containing the motor(s) that is (or are) being characterized. */
154    public final Mechanism mechanism;
155
156    /** The name of the mechanism being tested. */
157    public final String name;
158
159    /**
160     * Create a new mechanism specification for a SysId routine.
161     *
162     * @param drive Sends the SysId-specified drive signal to the mechanism motors during test
163     *     routines.
164     * @param log Returns measured data of the mechanism motors during test routines. To return
165     *     data, call `motor(string motorName)` on the supplied `SysIdRoutineLog` instance, and then
166     *     call one or more of the chainable logging handles (e.g. `voltage`) on the returned
167     *     `MotorLog`. Multiple motors can be logged in a single callback by calling `motor`
168     *     multiple times.
169     * @param mechanism The mechanism containing the motor(s) that is (or are) being characterized.
170     *     Will be declared as a requirement for the returned test commands.
171     * @param name The name of the mechanism being tested. Will be appended to the log entry title
172     *     for the routine's test state, e.g. "sysid-test-state-mechanism". Defaults to the name of
173     *     the mechanism if left null.
174     */
175    public SysIdMechanism(
176        Consumer<Voltage> drive, Consumer<SysIdRoutineLog> log, Mechanism mechanism, String name) {
177      this.drive = drive;
178      this.log = log != null ? log : _ -> {};
179      this.mechanism = mechanism;
180      this.name = name != null ? name : mechanism.getName();
181    }
182
183    /**
184     * Create a new mechanism specification for a SysId routine. The name of the routine is
185     * generated based on the name of the given mechanism.
186     *
187     * @param drive Sends the SysId-specified drive signal to the mechanism motors during test
188     *     routines.
189     * @param log Returns measured data of the mechanism motors during test routines. To return
190     *     data, call `motor(string motorName)` on the supplied `SysIdRoutineLog` instance, and then
191     *     call one or more of the chainable logging handles (e.g. `voltage`) on the returned
192     *     `MotorLog`. Multiple motors can be logged in a single callback by calling `motor`
193     *     multiple times.
194     * @param mechanism The mechanism containing the motor(s) that is (or are) being characterized.
195     *     Will be declared as a requirement for the returned test commands. The mechanism's `name`
196     *     will be appended to the log entry title for the routine's test state, e.g.
197     *     "sysid-test-state-mechanism".
198     */
199    public SysIdMechanism(
200        Consumer<Voltage> drive, Consumer<SysIdRoutineLog> log, Mechanism mechanism) {
201      this(drive, log, mechanism, null);
202    }
203  }
204
205  /** Motor direction for a SysId test. */
206  public enum Direction {
207    /** Forward. */
208    FORWARD,
209    /** Reverse. */
210    REVERSE
211  }
212
213  /**
214   * Returns a command to run a quasistatic test in the specified direction.
215   *
216   * <p>The command will call the `drive` and `log` callbacks supplied at routine construction once
217   * per iteration. Upon command end or interruption, the `drive` callback is called with a value of
218   * 0 volts.
219   *
220   * @param direction The direction in which to run the test.
221   * @return A command to run the test.
222   */
223  public Command quasistatic(Direction direction) {
224    double outputSign =
225        switch (direction) {
226          case FORWARD -> 1.0;
227          case REVERSE -> -1.0;
228        };
229    State state =
230        switch (direction) {
231          case FORWARD -> State.QUASISTATIC_FORWARD;
232          case REVERSE -> State.QUASISTATIC_REVERSE;
233        };
234
235    return m_mechanism
236        .mechanism
237        .run(
238            co -> {
239              Timer timer = Timer.createStarted();
240              while (!timer.hasElapsed(m_config.timeout)) {
241                m_mechanism.drive.accept(
242                    (Voltage) m_config.rampRate.times(Seconds.of(timer.get() * outputSign)));
243                m_mechanism.log.accept(this);
244                m_recordState.accept(state);
245                co.yield();
246              }
247            })
248        .whenExited(this::stopRoutine)
249        .named("sysid-" + state + "-" + m_mechanism.name);
250  }
251
252  /**
253   * Returns a command to run a dynamic test in the specified direction.
254   *
255   * <p>The command will call the `drive` and `log` callbacks supplied at routine construction once
256   * per iteration. Upon command end or interruption, the `drive` callback is called with a value of
257   * 0 volts.
258   *
259   * @param direction The direction in which to run the test.
260   * @return A command to run the test.
261   */
262  public Command dynamic(Direction direction) {
263    double outputSign =
264        switch (direction) {
265          case FORWARD -> 1.0;
266          case REVERSE -> -1.0;
267        };
268    State state =
269        switch (direction) {
270          case FORWARD -> State.DYNAMIC_FORWARD;
271          case REVERSE -> State.DYNAMIC_REVERSE;
272        };
273
274    return m_mechanism
275        .mechanism
276        .run(
277            co -> {
278              Voltage output = m_config.stepVoltage.times(outputSign);
279              Timer timer = Timer.createStarted();
280              while (!timer.hasElapsed(m_config.timeout)) {
281                m_mechanism.drive.accept(output);
282                m_mechanism.log.accept(this);
283                m_recordState.accept(state);
284                co.yield();
285              }
286            })
287        .whenExited(this::stopRoutine)
288        .named("sysid-" + state + "-" + m_mechanism.name);
289  }
290
291  private void stopRoutine() {
292    m_mechanism.drive.accept(Volts.of(0));
293    m_recordState.accept(State.NONE);
294  }
295}
